import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Year': [1990, 1992, 1995, 1998, 2000, 2003, 2005, 2008, 2010, 2013, 2015, 2018, 2020],
    'Infant Mortality (Female)': [28.0, 27.2, 25.5, 23.8, 22.5, 21.2, 20.0, 18.1, 16.0, 15.0, 14.0, 13.2, 12.5],
    'Infant Mortality (Male)': [32.0, 30.8, 29.0, 26.7, 24.5, 23.3, 22.0, 20.2, 18.5, 17.5, 16.5, 15.8, 15.0],
    'Neonatal Mortality': [19.5, 19.6, 19.3, 19.5, 19.5, 19.2, 19.0, 18.7, 18.5, 18.2, 18.0, 17.7, 17.5],
    'Under-5 Mortality (Female)': [35.0, 34.0, 32.0, 30.0, 28.0, 26.2, 24.5, 22.0, 20.0, 19.0, 18.0, 17.0, 16.0],
    'Under-5 Mortality (Male)': [40.0, 38.5, 36.5, 34.2, 32.0, 30.3, 28.5, 26.0, 24.0, 23.0, 22.0, 21.0, 20.0]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
df_melted = df.melt(id_vars=['Year'],
                    value_vars=['Infant Mortality (Female)', 'Infant Mortality (Male)',
                                'Neonatal Mortality', 'Under-5 Mortality (Female)'],
                    var_name='Category', value_name='Rate')

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
palette = sns.color_palette("husl", n_colors=5)

ax = sns.lineplot(data=df_melted, x='Year', y='Rate', hue='Category', palette=palette, linewidth=2.5)
ax = sns.scatterplot(data=df_melted, x='Year', y='Rate', hue='Category', palette=palette, s=60, edgecolor='w', linewidth=0.8)

for line in ax.lines[:5]:
    x, y = line.get_xydata().T
    ax.fill_between(x, y, color=line.get_color(), alpha=0.2)

plt.title('Child Mortality Trends in Jordan (1990-2020)', fontsize=16, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Year', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Mortality Rate (per 1,000 live births)', fontsize=12)
plt.legend(title='Mortality Category', title_fontsize=12, fontsize=10, frameon=True, framealpha=1)
plt.xticks(fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)
plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig('output.png')


--- SUMMARY ---
 The image is a line chart with shaded areas illustrating the trends in child mortality rates in Jordan from 1990 to 2020. The chart is titled "Child Mortality Trends in Jordan (1990-2020)" and displays mortality rates per 1,000 live births on the vertical axis, ranging from 0 to 40, while the horizontal axis marks the years from 1990 to 2020.

Five distinct categories of child mortality are represented, each with a unique color and corresponding shaded area beneath the line to emphasize the trend over time. The categories include Infant Mortality (Female) depicted in a reddish hue, Infant Mortality (Male) in greenish-yellow, Neonatal Mortality in teal, Under-5 Mortality (Female) in blue, and Under-5 Mortality (Male) in purple.

Starting in 1990, the highest mortality rate is observed in Under-5 Mortality (Male) at 40 per 1,000 live births, followed closely by Under-5 Mortality (Female) at 35. Infant Mortality (Male) begins at 32, while Infant Mortality (Female) starts at 28, and Neonatal Mortality remains relatively stable at around 19.5. Over the three decades, all categories exhibit a downward trend. By 2020, the Under-5 Mortality (Male) rate decreases to 20, and the Under-5 Mortality (Female) rate falls to 16. Infant Mortality (Male) reduces to 15, and Infant Mortality (Female) drops to 12.5, with Neonatal Mortality showing a more modest decline to 17.5.

The data points are marked with circular symbols for each year, allowing for clear observation of the specific values at those intervals. The chart effectively highlights a consistent reduction in child mortality rates across all categories over the 30-year period.
